inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted-average count from the Q2 2026 10-Q (SEC XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, period ended 2026-06-30); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in owner FCF -- charging both would double-count. Count fell from 1,495.0M (Q1 2026) to 1,474.8M (Q2 2026) on the $2.0B H1-2026 buyback.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement, ShareBasedCompensation add-back ($299M), which is the company's own combined P&L SBC expense figure; BSX does not separately disclose cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement in a distinct XBRL tag post-2015, so no further addition was made to avoid double-counting an unquantified amount
inputs.wacc_rationale: Large-cap, investment-grade US medtech; risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST), ERP ~5%, beta ~1.0-1.1 given moderate cyclicality and elevated near-term execution risk (cyberattack, WATCHMAN/PFA competitive pressure) -> cost of equity ~9.3%; blended with ~15% debt weight at an after-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (2025 InterestExpense $349M / total debt $12.6B pretax ~2.8%, x(1-20%) effective tax) gives WACC ~8.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- BSX's balance sheet does not carry a separately disclosed operating-lease liability large enough to change net debt; no lease adjustment applied
inputs.nci_treatment: not applicable -- no material minority interest reported
inputs.notes: Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md: profitable, growing, diversified US operating company (medical devices) -> standard owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year explicit horizon per section 2(d) because the FY2025 owner-FCF margin (16.7%) is still below its projected mature level (~19-20% base case) as EBITDA margin continues to expand off the FY2026 restructuring program. Interest-income strip does NOT apply: BSX carries net debt (~$12.1B), not net cash -- InvestmentIncomeInterest is not a disclosed XBRL tag for this filer and total debt >> cash throughout the history. Base-year (FY2026, Y1) growth set at 5.0%, below the company's own 5-6% FY2026 organic guidance, to reflect the August 2026 cyberattack disruption that management has said makes both Q3 and full-year guidance unlikely to be met; H1-2026 reported growth was 9.5% YoY but decelerated to 7.5% in Q2 alone before the attack. First DCF build for this ticker -- no prior valuation to reconcile against.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue (15.2%), FCF (28.4%) and EPS (63.3%, off a near-zero FY2020 base) 5yr/3yr CAGRs are far above the 5yr equity CAGR of 9.8%, driven by a structural EBITDA-margin expansion (10.5% in FY2020 to 24.8% in FY2025) as the company scaled Farapulse/WATCHMAN and absorbed prior-year one-offs (FY2020 was a COVID-depressed trough with a net loss). Equity CAGR is used as the conservative anchor for historical context, but the forward base case does not extrapolate the FY2022-2025 owner-FCF CAGR (67%) -- that period captured a one-time margin inflection that is not repeatable at the same rate; FY2026 growth is instead anchored to guidance and current deceleration evidence.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF grew from $962M (FY2020) to $3,359M (FY2025), a 5yr CAGR of 28.4% -- faster than revenue's 15.2%, reflecting margin expansion rather than SBC growing faster than cash flow (SBC itself grew only from $170M to $299M over the same period, roughly in line with revenue).

base.narrative: FY2026 growth lands near the low end of guidance (~5%) as the August cyberattack disruption and WATCHMAN standalone/PFA competitive softness weigh on the year, then reaccelerates to 6.5-7% in FY2027-28 as FARAWATCH concomitant procedures, WATCHMAN FLX Pro, TAVR/IVL and the SoniVie renal-denervation entry ramp, before decelerating toward a 3% terminal rate as the med-tech category matures. EBITDA margin expands from 25.5% to a 27.5% plateau as the ~$500M restructuring program (targeted by 2029) offsets ongoing PFA/WATCHMAN pricing pressure. Cash tax rate normalizes modestly above the unusually low FY2025 print (14.6%) toward a 20% steady state.

bull.narrative: Cyberattack disruption proves transient (contained within Q3 2026, no lasting customer-relationship damage), WATCHMAN FLX Pro and FARAWATCH successfully offset standalone-procedure softness, and Farapulse holds share as the PFA category keeps expanding rather than simply reallocating between incumbents. Restructuring savings drop straight to the bottom line ahead of schedule, TAVR/IVL and the SoniVie renal-denervation platform become genuine new growth legs, and further disciplined tuck-in M&A (in the Bolt Medical/SoniVie mold) adds incremental platforms without diluting returns.

bear.narrative: The cyberattack disruption extends into 2027 (customer order-processing/shipping relationships take longer to rebuild than management expects), WATCHMAN standalone volumes keep deteriorating as OCEAN/CHAMPION-AF trial data permanently narrows the eligible patient pool, and Medtronic/J&J/Abbott PFA platforms continue taking share faster than Farapulse can defend it in an already ~80%-penetrated US market. Two guidance cuts in a single year (2026) prove to be a pattern rather than a one-off, restructuring charges run ahead of realized savings through the 2029 target, and margin compresses as pricing pressure in electrophysiology and LAAC intensifies.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 growth lands near the low end of guidance (~5%) as the cyberattack and WATCHMAN/PFA softness weigh on the year, reaccelerating to 6.5-7% in FY2027-28 on FARAWATCH, WATCHMAN FLX Pro, TAVR/IVL and SoniVie, then decelerating to a 3% terminal rate. EBITDA margin expands to a 27.5% plateau as restructuring savings largely offset competitive pricing pressure.
scenario_narratives.bull: Cyberattack disruption proves transient and contained to Q3 2026; WATCHMAN FLX Pro/FARAWATCH and continued PFA category expansion (not just share reallocation) sustain high-single/low-double-digit growth for several years; restructuring savings arrive ahead of schedule and further disciplined tuck-in M&A adds new platforms.
scenario_narratives.bear: Cyberattack fallout extends into 2027, WATCHMAN standalone volumes keep deteriorating post-OCEAN/CHAMPION-AF, and PFA share losses to Medtronic/J&J/Abbott continue faster than expected; two 2026 guidance cuts prove to be a pattern, restructuring charges run ahead of savings, and margin compresses under pricing pressure.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the house default 15% to 25% given two guidance cuts within 2026 alone, an unresolved cyberattack whose duration and financial magnitude management itself says are still uncertain, and clear evidence (OCEAN/CHAMPION-AF trial data, ~80%-penetrated PFA market) that the WATCHMAN and electrophysiology slowdowns are structural, not merely a one-quarter disruption. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default) to match, since the bull case requires several distinct things to go right simultaneously (cyberattack fully transient, PFA share defended, restructuring ahead of schedule) rather than one. Base retained at 50% as the balance sheet carries no solvency risk (investment-grade, net debt/EBITDA ~2.1x) and the company remains a share leader in structurally growing categories even amid the current execution wobble.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Boston Scientific is a diversified, innovation-driven medtech compounder (Farapulse PFA, WATCHMAN LAAC, TAVR/IVL, renal denervation) working through a genuine, acknowledged rough patch in 2026 -- two guidance cuts, a cyberattack that has disrupted Q3 operations, and faster-than-expected competitive share losses in its two highest-profile franchises (WATCHMAN standalone, Farapulse PFA). None of this reads as a going-concern issue: the balance sheet is investment-grade, EBITDA margins have expanded steadily for five straight years, and the company continues to convert minority stakes in innovative device startups (Bolt Medical, SoniVie) into full ownership. The valuation therefore keeps the base case as a still-growing, margin-expanding compounder, but widens the bear weighting materially to reflect that the two acute 2026 problems (WATCHMAN patient-selection uncertainty, PFA competitive intensity) look structural rather than one-quarter noise, and that the cyberattack's full financial impact remains genuinely unknown as of the valuation date.
key_risks_to_valuation: Unquantified financial magnitude and duration of the August 2026 cyberattack -- Q3/FY2026 results have not yet been reported as of this valuation
WATCHMAN standalone procedure deceleration may be a durable shift in physician referral patterns (OCEAN/CHAMPION-AF), not a temporary air pocket
PFA category is already ~80% penetrated in the US with Medtronic, J&J and Abbott all gaining share -- Farapulse's growth runway may be narrower than the base case assumes
Two guidance cuts within a single year raise a real question about near-term forecasting visibility into core franchise trends
Restructuring plan (~$500M annual savings targeted by 2029) carries execution risk and near-term cash/charge drag ($700-800M pre-tax charges, $600-700M cash outlays through 2029)
Continued M&A pace (Bolt Medical, SoniVie) adds integration and contingent-consideration risk on top of already-softening organic growth
